title: Bina and tevuna: grasping a concept, and drawing it up to others
overview: *Bina* has two levels. *Bina* itself goes down into a concept and understands it; *tevuna* is the light of *bina* spreading out, and it comes from *kelita*, going over the matter again even after it is understood. The man of *bina* goes down into the deep well and drinks; the man of *tevuna* brings the water up to the sheep, as the Mitteler Rebbe brings this book's depth to us. Without *tevuna* the understanding stays where it is: the Greeks had a steam turbine and never applied it, and a scholar can master a whole *pilpul* and still not rule guilty or innocent. *Bina* has emotions of its own, but there is always another hand; it takes a man of *tevuna*, who has absorbed the matter, to decide. *Tevuna* is *ben u'vas*, the lower mother that gives birth to the *middos* through *daas*, while *bina* is the grandmother. And what carries *bina* over into *tevuna* is *bina sheb'bina*, the one power in your hands: the hundred and first time makes an *oved*. *Hisbonenus* is *avoda*, and the goal is to get fired up.

sections.title: Tevuna is bina spreading out, and it comes from going over it once more
sections.summary: *Bina* has two levels, *bina* and *tevuna*. *Tevuna* is the light of *bina* spreading out, and it comes from *kelita*: going over a matter again even after it is understood well, so that the man of *tevuna* can draw the deep waters up to others.

phrases.he: (ב) והנה ידוע שיש בבינה עצמה ב' מדרגות, בינה ותבונה,
phrases.en: And in *bina* there's two levels: *bina* and *tevuna*.

phrases.he: וענין התבונה הוא בחינת התפשטות אור הבינה
(כמו שכתוב בזהר דאבא ואמא תתאין הם ישראל סבא ותבונה,
ונקרא אימא תתאה כו')
phrases.en: *Tevuna* is called the lower mother.

blocks.text: *Bina* has two levels, *bina* and *tevuna*: analysis, and the spreading out of its light when the concept is well absorbed. In the *Zohar*, *tevuna* is *Ima tata'a* (the lower mother), with *Yisroel Saba*.

phrases.he: מצד קליטתה היטב בכלי המקבל ההשגה דבינה,
phrases.en: It gets absorbed into the *kli hamekabel* of the *hasaga*, into your brain.

phrases.he: על כן מתפשט בה להביאה בכמה ענינים נבדלים מעצם ההשגה,
phrases.en: Then it can spread out and it can go into various things that are separate from the actual understanding itself.

phrases.he: והוא הנקרא איש תבונה,
phrases.en: And that's what's called an *ish tevuna*,

phrases.he: כמו מים עמוקים כו' איש תבונה ידלנה.
phrases.en: the *ish tevuna* can draw out the deep waters.

blocks.text: This too comes *davka* from *hisbonenus* (contemplation). Stop once you understand it and you have *bina* without *tevuna*; keep going over it and it is absorbed into your brain, and can spread into things separate from the understanding itself.
That is the *ish tevuna* (man of *tevuna*) of the verse, who can draw out the deep waters.

phrases.he: מים עמוקים הם בחינת עמקות בינה שנשאר בהעלם העצמיות,
phrases.en: The real depth of the *bina*, which remains in the *helem ha'atzmiyus* of the concept itself.

phrases.he: ואיש תבונה דווקא ידלנה
phrases.en: *Davka* the *ish tevuna*, *davka* the Mitteler Rebbe, can draw it out,

phrases.he: וישאבנה מן ההעלם
phrases.en: and he draws it out from the *helem*,

phrases.he: להביאה להתפשטות בכמה אופנים שונים
לרוות את המקבלים

blocks.text: The real depth stays hidden in the essence of the concept, as much of what this book discusses stays hidden in itself.
As always, the book is a *mashal* (analogy) on itself: the man of *tevuna*, the Mitteler Rebbe, draws the depth out of hiding for the thirsty receivers: us.

sections.title: The deep well: the man of bina goes down to the water, the man of tevuna brings it up to the sheep
sections.summary: The man of *bina* goes down into the well and drinks there; the man of *tevuna* brings the water up to the sheep, as the Mitteler Rebbe brings this book's depth to us. *Tevuna* is a power that spreads out from *bina*: of the two, *bina* is the width and *tevuna* the length.

phrases.he: כמו הדולה מים עמוקים להשקות הצאן כו'
phrases.en: Like, for instance, somebody who draws out very deep water from a well in order to give drink to the sheep.

phrases.he: והוא כמו שאנו רואים בחוש,
phrases.en: Like we see in actuality:

phrases.he: שבהיות השכל והסברא עמוקים ביותר מהכיל בהשגת אדם,
הנקרא מים עמוקים כו',
שהוא בחינת עומק המושג הנזכר לעיל
שהאורך והרוחב ממנו בא כו'

blocks.title: Throw the sheep in, or bring the water up
blocks.text: Water is drawn from a deep well for the sheep: throw each sheep into the well, or bring the water up. The man of *bina* goes down and drinks there himself, which does not help the sheep; the man of *tevuna* brings the water up, from deep to shallow.

Here too the book is a *mashal* on itself: its deep waters, the *taalumos chachma* (hidden depths of wisdom), are the aquifer, and a well's water stays in the aquifer: the depth of the concept, source of its length and width.

phrases.he: ואיש בעל תבונה דווקא ידלנה,
phrases.en: *Davka* the *ish tevuna*, over here the Mitteler Rebbe, can draw it out, like from a well.

phrases.he: פירוש שיוציא לאור בחינת העלם העומק המושג
phrases.en: He'll bring out to the outer light that hidden *omek hamusag*,

phrases.he: עד שיכילנו השגת האדם,
phrases.en: until a regular person, who doesn't have such a deep mind like the Mitteler Rebbe, like us,

phrases.he: כאלו לא היה עמוק כלל,
phrases.en: as if it was not deep at all.

phrases.he: כמו הדולה מים עמוקים שמקרב את העומק כו'
phrases.en: Like a guy who draws out the deep water from the well, which means basically from the aquifer, that he brings the *omek* close to the sheep.

blocks.text: *Davka* the man of *tevuna*, here the Mitteler Rebbe, draws it up like water from a well and brings the hidden depth into the light, until a regular person, without the Mitteler Rebbe's deep mind, can grasp it. Like us.

We lack the *daas* to learn even *Ayin Beis* properly, and great earlier minds could not go this deep. We get it because the man of *tevuna* brought it up to us, like water to the sheep: as if it were not deep at all.
Deep, yes, but by the measure of Americans: a regular college student could learn it with a little explanation, like our *New and Improved Kabbalah* series.
He draws up the deep waters from the aquifer and brings the depth close to the sheep.

phrases.he: ולפי זה מוכרח לומר
שכח התבונה הוא כח המתפשט מכח הבינה
phrases.en: The *koach hatevuna* is a power that spreads out from the *koach habina*,

phrases.he: להביא עומקה לגילוי למטה למקבלים כו'
phrases.en: to be able to bring the depth downward to the *mekablim*.

blocks.text: *Bina* itself does not draw the water out of the aquifer; it goes down into it, like a guy with a drill, and drinks down in the depth.
*Tevuna* spreads out from *bina*: without understanding into the thing you cannot bring it out. *Bina* comes first, and then its depth is brought into revelation below, to the receivers.

Between the two, *tevuna* is the *orech* (length) and *bina* the *rochav* (width). The length of *bina* is the power to explain it to yourself; the length of *tevuna*, to explain it to somebody else. Each has its own width and length, but of the two, *bina* is the width, spreading into all the parts. Against *chachma*, *bina* is the length; within *bina*, *tevuna* is.

blocks.title: The two Leviathans
blocks.text: That is the secret of the two Leviathans. *Hisbonenus* has two *nuns*, the straight and the bent, and there is a straight serpent and a crooked serpent. The crooked one, the female, was killed; the straight one, the male, was left alive but neutered, or *tevuna* could somehow have had babies even without the female.
Hence *davka* *tevuna* was left. The real *bina* is pretty much gone; what people have, and learn, is mostly the applications of the physical world: *tevuna*.

sections.title: The tafsan: a fine grasp that never comes out, like the Greeks
sections.summary: A man can be strong in *bina*, a good grasper, and still nothing comes out of his understanding, neither an application nor an explanation to anyone else. Whole societies are like this: the Greeks had the ideas and never applied them; the Americans are not so much understanders as appliers.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן כשאינו איש תבונות,
phrases.en: When he's not an *ish tevunos*,

phrases.he: גם שהוא בעל השגה במוח דבינה
(שנקרא תפסן בלשון העולם)
phrases.en: (*tafsan*: a chapper)

phrases.he: יוכל להיות שהשגתו נשארת רק כמו שהיא בעצם, במוח הבינה שלו
phrases.en: He understands it, but his understanding stays just the way it is.

phrases.he: שנקרא רוח בינתו לבד,
phrases.en: His own understanding only,

phrases.he: ולא יבוא ממנה שום התפשטות למטה בענין נבדל שחוץ מן עצם ההשגה כלל
phrases.en: and it will not come out into any kind of application, for instance, or any kind of explanation to somebody else, outside the *etzem hahasaga*.

blocks.text: Not so one who masters *bina* but is not a man of *tevunos*: a *tafsan*, "a chapper", with a good chap on the thing. His understanding stays as it is: he drinks the water, having gone down into the depth.
His own understanding only: it comes out into nothing outside the grasp itself, no application and no explanation to somebody else.

blocks.title: The Greeks' steam turbine
blocks.text:
So too with societies. Greek power was a power of *bina*; American power is *davka* *tevuna*: "They're not so much understanders, but appliers."

The Greeks had a steam turbine; there is one in the museum. But their philosophers sat and thought, and like men of *bina* never thought of running an appliance on it, though the technology was there two thousand years ago. They knew oil from the ground burns, and never applied that either.

blocks.title: They could have had an Industrial Revolution
blocks.text: America's specialty, and the modern West's, is airplanes, trains, cars, electricity. The Greeks knew electricity, the wheel and metal, and had a turbine engine: they could have had the Industrial Revolution two thousand years ago. Modern people are not so smart: the Greeks did the thinking; we apply it.

A lot of these thoughts were available already before, and as a matter of fact, compared to them, people nowadays are kind of low style: they only think about bread and butter. The reason the Greeks never thought of the application is that they never even thought on such a low level; for them it was all intellectual, pure intellect: the pursuit of intellect, not the pursuit of the dollar.

sensitivity.reason: Calls people of today, and by implication Americans, low-style people who only think about bread and butter and the dollar.
sensitivity.publishable: A lot of these thoughts were available already before. The reason the Greeks never thought of the application is that for them it was all intellectual, pure intellect: the pursuit of intellect, and not of its uses.

blocks.text: America pursues applications. The old world knew the theory of flight: it had kites, saw birds fly and had an idea of how it worked, but never put it together, because it was into *bina* and had nothing to do with *tevuna*.
So a person, even a whole society, can keep it all in the *bina*, though a bigger master of *bina* than the master of *tevuna*.

The Wright brothers and Edison were not on the Greek philosophers' intellectual level. A Greek philosopher would have thought any of them a *grober mentsh* (a coarse person), even a lowlife: thinking about a better horse carriage instead of refined, upper things.
Yet the advances in *tevuna* too come from *bina sheb'bina* (*bina* within *bina*), the analysis, though a person may have more *tevuna* than *bina*.

phrases.he: וגם שיש בהשגה אורך ורוחב ועומק כנזכר לעיל,
הכל הוא רק בעצם ההשגה, כמו שהיא,
אבל לא שיתגלה למטה בענין נבדל,
ומכל שכן עומק המושג הרי נשאר בעומקו בהעלם לעצמו,
phrases.en: And especially the *omek hamusag* stays deep inside of itself.

phrases.he: וכן האורך והרוחב,
phrases.en: Even the length and the width,

phrases.he: הכל בעצם ההשגה כמו שהיא, שהיא במקומה לבד

blocks.text: Even explaining downward, the length, is here mostly to himself; explaining to others is *tevuna*, and so is revealing a thing in a separate matter, the whole matter of a *mashal*.
All the more the depth stays hidden in itself. The Greek philosophers produced nothing from it, and did not even explain it to regular people.

That is another thing. In America the whole thing is that you have to explain it to everybody, everybody should understand. Even a stupid guy has to go to school and learn it. Over there it was just for the elite. A few elite were happy to think about these things, and they never thought they should explain it to the guy working in the marketplace.

sensitivity.reason: Calls the ordinary person who must be schooled "a stupid guy".
sensitivity.publishable: That is another thing. In America the whole thing is that you have to explain it to everybody, everybody should understand. Even the simplest person has to go to school and learn it. Over there it was just for the elite. A few elite were happy to think about these things, and they never thought they should explain it to the guy working in the marketplace.

blocks.text: So length and width are all in the grasp itself.

sections.title: The Talmudic debate that yields no ruling: an idea that is only hiyuli
sections.summary: One can master a whole *pilpul* and still be unable to bring out of it a ruling of guilty or innocent; a concept by itself is only *hiyuli*, and "you can't do nothing with it". The power of *tevuna* brings the grasp down into a separate matter: a ruling, an arousal of the heart, thought in many ways.

phrases.he: ודוגמא לכל זה,
הנה אנו רואים בעומק הפלפול בתלמוד
וטעמים בסברות רבות כך וכך
גם שבאים בהשגה דבינה,
אבל לא יוכלו עדיין להוציא לאור מעצם השכל
איזה פסק דין חייב או זכאי כלל

blocks.text: Some people follow a whole *pilpul* (Talmudic debate) with all its *sevaros* (lines of reasoning) and still cannot bring out of it a ruling of guilty or innocent.
In a way *tevuna* has the higher root: bringing a thing out takes understanding deeper than the original.

In one way the Greek philosophers were greater than modern scientists, whom they would call *grobe mentshen* (coarse people). But applying it gave the moderns the deeper understanding: we are no great theoreticians, but because we applied it we understand the principles better.

blocks.title: Archimedes and the eureka
blocks.text: Even the famous smart Greek is a story of *tevuna*: Archimedes, a thinker who applied nothing, until the king had a problem that needed an application. *Davka* because he had to apply it, he understood deeper, eureka: the displacement of water according to the mass.
Many understand the Talmud; the great *poskim* (halachic authorities), like the Rambam, could apply it to a ruling.

phrases.he: דהיינו שלא יוכל להוציא מתוך הסברה
איזה חיוב על פי זה השכל
ולא איזה זכות על פי זה השכל
כי עדיין אין השכל והסברה רק השכלה שכליות לבד,
בלתי ימצא ממנו שום התפשטות בהטיות לענין נבדל הימנה,
שהוא לחייב על ידה או לזכות על ידה

blocks.text: You can learn any subject in the Talmud and still not be able to *pasken* (rule) on it.
Finding guilty or innocent is *chesed* and *gevura* (kindness and severity), and they come *davka* from *tevuna*, not from *bina*.

phrases.he: והרי זה כמו דבר ההיולי
phrases.en: And it's just a *hiyuli*.

phrases.he: שלא נודע עדיין מה ימצא ממנה ומה יעשה בה
phrases.en: It's just like an idea, but nobody knows what will come out of it and what he can do with it.

phrases.he: (בל"א דער מושכל אליין כמו שהוא
ער קאן מיט אים נישט טאן קיין זאך
phrases.en: He can't do nothing with it,

phrases.he: ניט צו קערין לזכות או לחוב כו')
phrases.en: to be *noteh* to either *zechus* or *chiyuv*.)

blocks.text: It is just a *hiyuli*, an idea; nobody knows what will come of it. As it is, **he can't do nothing with it**, to lean to merit or guilt.

phrases.he: ואמנם כח התבונה שמתפשט ממוח הבינה,
היינו מה שביכולתו להביא עצם ההשגה
לבחינת התפשטות למטה ממנה
בכל ענין נבדל הימנה,
או לחיוב או לזכות
או להתפעל בלב,
וכן להביאה במחשבה בכמה אופנים שונים כו'.

blocks.text: Or to be aroused in the heart, knowing *hispaalus* (arousal) will come of it; or to bring it into thought. Here he starts what comes later: the letters of thought come from *Malchus* of *tevuna*.

So far: *tevuna* is *bina*'s power to spread out, bringing the grasp down into separate matters and into the *middos* (emotions). But it can also go up, as *bina* can: *tevuna* is a full *bina* by itself.

blocks.text: *Chachma sheb'bina* (*chachma* within *bina*) actually originates in *tevuna*. It discovers a new thing off to the side within the same thing: a length that, going up, comes out as a width. And the *chachma* of *bina* relates to the *bina* of *chachma*, understanding one thing from another, which is also *tevuna*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 019 opens by going back over the definition of tevuna before it reads the next line; placed after the last line of class 018.

blocks.text: And a *bina sheb'chachma* is called a *navon*, a person of *tevuna*, not a *mevin chacham*: understanding something from inside something is *tevuna* going up.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 019 opens by going back over the definition of tevuna before it reads the next line; placed after the last line of class 018.

blocks.text: *Bina sheb'bina* activates all the powers, *tevuna* included, by going over it until there is *kelita* (absorption). He listed the levels going up; now, going down: *chachma sheb'bina*, a new thing within the concept, comes from the *kelita*, not from *bina*, which understands only the concept itself. The height, going up, is different again; all of it is the light of *bina* spreading into other things.

blocks.text: The chapter's first sentence shows it: *tevuna* is the spreading of the light of *bina*. Not the spreading down; spreading, in every direction.

sections.title: The emotions within bina, and the man of tevuna who comes to a decision
sections.summary: *Bina* has emotions of its own, the intellect leaning toward merit or guilt, but they are still intellect, and in *bina* there is always another hand. Bringing them out into a final decision or a halachic ruling takes a man of *tevuna*, who has absorbed the matter.

phrases.he: אך לכאורה אנו רואים שיש בבינה עצמה בחינת מדות
הנקרא ז׳ תחתונים דבינה,
ונקרא מדות שבשכל המטה כלפי זכות
או שכל מטה כלפי חוב כידוע
היינו כמו שהמדות שבשכל הן בעצם ההשגה עדיין בהעלם

blocks.text: Now something new: after the *Chabad* (intellect) of *bina*, its seven lower levels, the *middos* of *bina*, the forty-nine gates: intellect leaning toward merit or toward guilt. Analyzing something, you also decide whether it is good or bad.

Learning *Chassidus*, we also decide it is a good thing: intellect leaning toward merit, already a *midda* (an emotion), not the intellect of the *Chassidus* itself. That decision awakens the *daas* for the thing or against it.
Still hidden: not that you actually like it, only a mental decision that you should. The *middos* of the intellect are not *middos*; they are intellect.

phrases.he: אבל להביא בחינת התגלותן
בדבר נבדל,
phrases.en: into an actual *psak halacha*,

phrases.he: כמו להורות
בענין מקרה דבר מה
phrases.en: in an actual thing that happens,

phrases.he: על פי השכל והסברא הזאת,
להטות את המשפט של זה הענין
לחסד וגבורה שבו דוקא,
הרי איש תבונה דווקא
יוציא לאור מן המדות שבבינה כו'

blocks.title: Fiddler on the Roof: on the other hand
blocks.text: In *bina* there are forty-nine *middos*, or seven. As in *Fiddler on the Roof*: on the one hand it is good; on the other hand, from this *sevara*, bad; on the other hand, from that one, good. In the intellectual brain of *bina* "there's many other hands."
Saying what it finally is, a *psak halacha* (halachic ruling), takes *davka* a man of *tevuna*; later he explains that the real ruling comes from *daas*.

That is why women are indecisive, and cannot be rebbes, rabbis or *poskim*: a time has to come to decide, and that takes a strong *daas*. Not that they have less *daas* than a man; they have the same. But their *bina yeseira* (an extra measure of *bina*) messes it up: "They always come up with another hand", and cannot stop.

sensitivity.reason: Says women cannot be rabbis or poskim because their extra bina messes up their daas, and calls them indecisive.

blocks.title: The businessman who thinks too much
blocks.text: In business, a guy who thinks too much makes a poor businessman: you must decide without all the details, and in *bina* there is always another one. Details are infinite.

And that is why women, it is not that they can never make a decision, they can, but that is why they are *kalei daas* (light of *daas*): they always come up with another detail and cannot make that final decision. The mind of *daas* is the mind of *hataya* (tilting). In the *bina* it tells you all kinds of things, like this, like that, but finally you say, "Listen, I gotta make a decision already."

sensitivity.reason: Explains "kalei daas" as women always coming up with another detail and being unable to decide.

blocks.text: The decision comes almost from a feeling, though the *sevaros* of *bina* influence it.

blocks.title: Jumping without a parachute
blocks.text: Where the *sevaros* all weigh to one side, anybody can decide. Whether to jump out of an airplane without a parachute takes no intellect of *hataya* (tilting): "There ain't no other hands."

("Unless you're suicidal.") "Yeah, right. If you're suicidal, then the answer is yes. Also a very simple answer. If you say, 'I want to kill myself, should I jump out of the airplane now without a parachute?', the answer is yes. Because if you do this, you'll kill yourself. And if you're a normal person that doesn't want to kill himself, the answer is no."

sensitivity.reason: Jokes about a suicidal person deciding to jump.

blocks.text: The leaning intellect is needed where the balance is close, or where things cannot be known now and you need a feeling.
Deciding the halacha is *davka* the man of *tevuna*. The Rambam or the Rif learned it until they had the *kelita*: it became part of their brain, and so they can decide.

Nor only from a feeling, as with *shasik Rav* (Rav was silent), who decided without being able to explain, the decision coming from *chachma* with the brain of *daas* leaning to it. Usually they decide out of *tevuna*.

To bring the hidden *middos* of the intellect into a separate thing is an actual ruling on what happened. So *tevuna* is explanation, the water brought to the sheep, and application: not only in halacha but in doing, which the Greeks never did with their steam engine.

phrases.he: ואיש תבונות היינו כח הקולט בכי טוב לעצם ההשגה,
phrases.en: Means the absorption of the *hasaga*.

phrases.he: על כן מתפשטת ההשגה בו
לעשות ולהורות בה כמה ענינים נבדלים לגמרי
וגם ביכולתו להביא את עומק בינה לידי גילוי כנזכר לעיל
ודי למבין

blocks.text: A man of *tevunos* has absorbed the grasp, so it spreads out in him; *kelita* is the *Keser* (crown) of *tevuna*, and it comes from *hisbonenus*, the double *nun*: stop at understanding and you won't have no *kelita*.
So there are application and explanation, really three: the essence of *tevuna* is *kelita*, its power is spreading out, and generally it means downward, into application or explanation to others.

sections.title: Yisroel Saba and Tevuna: the emotions of the mind as they come out, and the root of the letters of thought
sections.summary: *Tevuna* is the *middos* of *bina* as they come out of *bina*, as *Yisroel Saba* is those of *chachma*, and each becomes a full *partzuf*. Its *Malchus* is the root of the letters of thought, *Leah*: still part of the mind itself, while thought is already a garment.

phrases.he: (והיינו בחינת אבא ואמא תתאין ישראל סבא ותבונה
ישראל סבא מדות דחכמה ותבונה מדות דבינה
אך באין בבחינת הגילוי לחוץ
ובחינת מלכות דתבונה הוא השכל הבא במחשבה
הנקרא אותיות מחשבת שכל
phrases.en: That's the letters of the *machshevas sechel*, the *machshava* how it is still in the *sechel*,

phrases.he: שהשכל מתלבש בה
והוא בחינת כלי חיצוני למחשבה עיונית
שהוא גלוי השגה דבינה עצמה מצד עצם השכל והסברא כו'
ומבחינת מלכות דתבונה נמשך שרש אותיות המחשבה עצמה
שנקרא לאה כו'
והוא ד' רבתי דאחד)

blocks.text: The lower father and mother, *Yisroel Saba* and *Tevuna*, are the *middos* of *chachma* and of *bina* coming out into revelation.

Not just the *middos* of *bina*, which can stay inside and never be applied: *tevuna* is those *middos* as they come out. The *Chabad* of *bina* stays totally inside. Yet *Yisroel Saba* and *Tevuna* become whole *partzufim* of ten *sefiros*: *tevuna* has a *Chabad* of its own.
*Malchus* of *tevuna* is the letters of the *machshevas sechel*, thought as it still is in the intellect; later he calls it *Leah*.

The *machshava iyunis* is the *iyun* (analysis) itself, inside the intellect, dressed in the *machshevas sechel*, its letters: "a very very refined distinction", and you cannot have one without the other. The *machshevas sechel* comes *davka* from *Malchus* of *tevuna*, which puts the inner *iyun* into a separate thing: letters, words and concepts.

blocks.question: So *Malchus* of *tevuna* is not actually *Leah* itself, only its root?
blocks.text: No: *Malchus* of *tevuna* is still the essence, the intellect itself as it comes out. *Leah* is already like *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, actual thought, speech and action; thought is a garment, while *Malchus* of *tevuna* is part of the body, the inner intellect.

blocks.title: Speech over the telephone
blocks.text: Right now we are talking. The letters of speech are a separate garment, only sounds: over the telephone they become squiggles of electricity, then squiggles of air, then electricity along the nerves. Speech came from thought, also letters, a more inner garment in the brain but still not part of the speaker: *kalvush yachlif* (like a garment, it changes). *Malchus* of *tevuna* is part of the body, the brain itself; *Leah* is already talking inside your head. All this is explained much later in the book.
*Malchus* of *tevuna*, which is called *Leah*, is the large *dalet* of *echad*.

sections.title: Ben u'vas: tevuna's three dimensions, and the lower mother who gives birth to the emotions
sections.summary: The letters of *tevuna* spell *ben u'vas*, son and daughter: the two sides of *daas* that bring the emotions. Its depth is *kelita*, its length is bringing the grasp down to teach and to act, its width is spreading it out in thought. *Bina* is only the grandmother; *tevuna* is the lower mother who actually gives birth to the *middos*.

phrases.he: וזהו שנקרא תבונה בן ובת כידוע,
להיות כי גם בתבונה יש ג' דברים,
עומק ואורך ורוחב.

blocks.text: Also later: the letters of *tevuna* break into *ben u'vas*, *chesed* and *gevura*, meaning *daas*, which splits into those two minds. So *daas* and the feeling of *middos* come *davka* from *tevuna*, the lower mother; *bina* brings children only through her.

phrases.he: העומק הוא עצם כח התבונה הזאת שבאותה ההשגה,
כמו שהיא בשעה שקולטת אותה כו'
ובה יוכל עומק ההשגה הנזכר לעיל לבוא לגלוי,
כנזכר לעיל בפסוק איש תבונה ידלנה כו'

blocks.title: Holding it, or soaking it up like a sponge
blocks.text: The depth is the *kelita*: not holding the thing from the outside but soaking it up like a sponge, so it becomes part of you.
*Davka* through this *kelita* the *omek hamusag* (depth of the concept) comes into revelation: "a man of *tevuna* will draw it out."

phrases.he: והאורך הוא ירידתה בענין אחר הנבדל,
phrases.en: Either the bringing down into a separate thing,

phrases.he: להורות בו ולעשות מעשים רבים על ידה כו'
phrases.en: either to teach somebody else, to explain, or else to apply: to do, to apply it into actual action.

phrases.he: והרוחב הוא בחינת התפשטות התבונה בעצם ההשגה,
להרחיבה במחשבה בכמה רבוי אופנים שונים
ולא כמו שהיא לבד כו'

blocks.text: The length brings it into a separate thing: **to teach** somebody else, or to put it into action.
So the width of *bina*, its *chachma*, really comes from the width of *tevuna*: only with the *kelita* does *bina* itself widen.
*Tevuna* also has a height, as he said before: from *kelita* you understand one thing from another, which only one who absorbs it can. So he is a *navon*, a master of *tevuna*, not a *mevin*.

phrases.he: ומה שכלולה התבונה מב''ן וב''ת,
היינו מה שמתבונה דוקא יולדו המדות בגלוי מהות בפני עצמם,
כי מבינה עצמה לא היו תולדות המדות
phrases.en: From *bina* itself there won't be a *toldah* of the actual *midda*,

phrases.he: אף על פי שנקרא אם הבנים כו'
phrases.en: even though it's called *em habanim*

phrases.he: (אבל היא אימא עילאה)
phrases.en: (it's the upper mother).

phrases.he: מה שאין כן התבונה נקרא אימא תתאה
להוליד המדות,
phrases.en: actually gave birth to the *middos*,

phrases.he: והוא בחינת ב''ן וב''ת, אהבה ויראה,
שבאים בהתכללות בתבונה דוקא,
שהיא בחינת התפשטות אור הבינה למטה כנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: From *tevuna*, through *daas*, *chesed* and *gevura* are born; from *bina*, with always another hand, they would not be. *Bina* is still "the mother of the children": without the first *hisbonenus* there is no *tevuna*.

blocks.title: Bina the grandmother
blocks.text: But it is the upper mother: a grandmother, the source but not the immediate one. *Bina* should be the *savta*, as *Yisroel Saba* is the grandfather; or *chachma* is grandfather and *bina* grandmother. *Bina* is the mother of *tevuna*, "the mother of the mother of the *middos*": of its own *middos*, which, coming out, are *tevuna*.
*Tevuna*, the lower mother, actually gives birth to the *middos*: in it all the other hands come together to bring out the final *midda*. In *bina* it is all pieces that cannot make a product.

Now he adds "downward": what we call *tevuna* is *davka* the downward spreading, the lower mother; its other spreadings have other names (*chachma* of *bina*, *bina* of *chachma*). And *tevuna*, like *chachma* and *bina*, has a source in *Arich*: the hidden *tevuna*.

sections.title: The intellect of the emotions comes from tevuna, and the point is to get fired up
sections.summary: The *mochin* of the *middos* come from *tevuna*, the go-between that carries the *uvchein* of *bina* into the heart. That is the whole point of *hisbonenus*: it is *avoda*, not intellect, and the goal is to get fired up, in the heart, in the mind, in the will, and in the very essence of the soul.

phrases.he: וגם לזה הטעם בחינת המוחין שבמדות נמשך מבחינת התבונה
phrases.en: And that's why the *mochin* of the *middos*, in other words the *mochin* of *Z"A*, comes from *tevuna*, not from *bina*.

phrases.he: (וכמו שכתוב יהו״ה בחכמה יסד ארץ,
דאבא יסד ברתא כו'
כונן שמים בתבונה,
שמים הן בחינת המדות, אש מים כידוע
וכן ובתבונה
יתכונן,
phrases.en: it'll be established,

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת קיום המדות בבחינת המוחין דתבונה שבהם,
כי התבונה כמו ממוצע להביא מוחין מבחינת מדות דבינה במדות שבלב

blocks.text: So the *mochin* of the *middos* come from *tevuna*, not *bina*. "*Havaya* founded the earth with *chachma*": Abba founded *Malchus*. "He established the heavens with *tevuna*": fire and water, *chesed* and *gevura*.

What does *tevuna* establish? The existence of the *middos*, through the *mochin* of *tevuna* in them. They come from the *middos* of *bina*, but to become the *mochin* of the *middos* they must pass through *tevuna*, the go-between.

This is the *uvchein* ("and so"): the *middos* of *bina* without its *Chabad*. *Avodas halev* (the service of the heart) brings only that end into the heart; in *avodas hamochin* (the service of the mind) the whole *Chabad* of *bina* comes in.

phrases.he: שזהו כמו כח ההבאה בענין הנבדל,
phrases.en: that is like to bring it into something different,

phrases.he: שהוא עיקר ענין התבונה כנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: Bringing it into a separate matter means bringing the intellect into the *midda*, something apart from the intellect. This power does various things: it teaches others, and it applies, and applying includes bringing the intellect into actual feeling.

He reads the line's end as "the main matter of *hisbonenus*": bringing it into the *middos*, as in *Kuntres HaHispaalus*. The goal is an *oved* (one who serves G-d), not a *maskil* (a person of intellect): *avoda*, not *haskala*.
blocks.outOfPlace: The tape ran out in the middle of this line; class 020 opens by finishing it.

blocks.text: Most people think learners of *Shaar HaYichud* or *Ayin Beis* are *maskilim* up in the *himmel* (heaven). A big mistake: *avoda* means to kvetch your face. *Daas*.
blocks.outOfPlace: The tape ran out in the middle of this line; class 020 opens by finishing it.

blocks.text: The whole *hisbonenus* is *tevuna*, because *daas*, the *ben u'vas* that brings about the *middos*, comes from *tevuna*, which makes the *middos* of *bina* the intellect of the *middos*.
blocks.outOfPlace: The tape ran out in the middle of this line; class 020 opens by finishing it.

blocks.text: All the Alter Rebbe wanted, he explained in *Kuntres HaHispaalus*, was *hispaalus Elokus* (excitement over G-dliness) in the chassidim: not finding *Arich* and *Atik* "so interesting", but getting fired up. That is *avodas halev*.
blocks.outOfPlace: The tape ran out in the middle of this line; class 020 opens by finishing it.

blocks.text: A bigger goal is *avodas hamochin*, the whole brain fired up, even the thought of *bina*. Higher still, in *Atik* and *Arich*: a hot *ratzon* (will) and *taanug* (delight) for it, a total addict, getting your *taanug* from it.
blocks.outOfPlace: The tape ran out in the middle of this line; class 020 opens by finishing it.

blocks.title: Chassidus instead of blood
blocks.text: Higher still is the *yechida* (essence of the soul): this is what I am. It is said that poking the Mitteler Rebbe with a needle would draw *Chassidus*, not blood; the soul is in the blood.
blocks.outOfPlace: The tape ran out in the middle of this line; class 020 opens by finishing it.

blocks.text: It goes as far as suffering for the *Chassidus*, higher than *taanug*, which wants it only when it gets it. The essence of the soul, *yechida*, is readiness to die for the sanctification of G-d's Name: even a simple Jew gives up everything, "because this is what I really am." It is the highest of the five levels whose *hispaalus* he explains there.
blocks.outOfPlace: The tape ran out in the middle of this line; class 020 opens by finishing it.

sections.title: The two nuns: hisbonenus, bina sheb'bina, carries bina over into tevuna
sections.summary: *Bina* has a bent *nun*, the width, and a straight *nun*, the length, and the *nun* is spelled with both. *Hisbonenus*, *bina sheb'bina*, joins *bina* to *tevuna* through the straight *nun*: going over the same explanation once more brings the *kelita*, as the hundred and first time makes an *oved*. It is the one power in your hands.

phrases.he: וידוע גם כן שיש נו''ן כפופה ונו''ן פשוטה בבינה,
phrases.en: In *bina* itself there's a *nun pshuta* and a *nun kfufa*,

phrases.he: להיות נו''ן כפופה הוא הרוחב
ונו''ן פשוטה הוא האורך
ונ' המלוי שלו בנ' פשוטה
phrases.en: The *milui* of *nun* is with a long *nun*.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן בשאר מילוי האותיות

blocks.text: In *bina*, and in *tevuna*, there is a straight *nun* and a bent *nun*; between the two, *bina* is the bent, the width, and *tevuna* the straight, the length. *Nun* is spelled *nun*, *vav*, *nun*, ending long.

blocks.question: Why does he say it is not so in the other letters? The mem also ends with a mem, the open mem and the closed one; and a vav ends with a vav.
blocks.text: The spelling of *nun* is *nun*, *vav*, *nun*: a bent *nun* and a straight one, connected. It means two things. In *mem*, the open and closed *mem* are two levels of one thing; here the *vav* both separates and unites them, since "and" means there are two things and that they are connected. So in *bina* there are two separate matters, not just two levels: *bina* and *tevuna*. And the length and the width are special things here too.

phrases.he: כי האורך נכלל ברוחב
phrases.en: because the length is included in the width.

phrases.he: וכך הוא בתבונה,
phrases.en: And the same thing in *tevuna*: there's a length and a width.

phrases.he: ואמנם נון הכפל בענין הנקרא התבוננות,
כמו עמי לא התבונן וכו',
שזהו בחינת פנימית בינה הנקרא עיון,
לעמוד על דבר כו'
שנקרא בינה שבבינה,
הוא ממוצע בין בינה לתבונה
phrases.en: The *hisbonenus* is the *emtza'i* between the two.

phrases.he: על ידי הנו''ן פשוטה,
phrases.en: through the *nun pshuta*, through the *orech* of *bina* itself,

phrases.he: שמחמתו נקרא התבוננות כו'
ודי למבין:

blocks.text: The length is included in the width: only with the width of the whole explanation in your head can you bring it down to others, in *tevuna* too. The doubled *nun* is *hisbonenus*, called *iyun*: going over a thing again and again to get to its bottom.

It is called *bina sheb'bina*, a double *nun*, the go-between of *bina* and *tevuna*, and it brings about the *kelita*. Once he has a chap on the intellect, how does he get to its *tevuna*, to apply it and teach it? By *hisbonenus*: learning it one more time. There is no special power of *kelita*.
So *bina sheb'bina* is the main power, the linchpin and the one in your hands; the others are not really.

Even the power of *daas*, which is partially in your hands, since you can force yourself to concentrate on something, really comes *davka* from *bina sheb'bina*. Even the *avoda zara*-niks (idolaters) who just meditate on a candle, or on the emptiness, do it because of an understanding they have. It is a wrong understanding, but what they are given first is an explanation, not a meditation, and they do it because they did a *hisbonenus*, an analysis of the thing.

blocks.title: The shevira begins in bina sheb'bina
blocks.text: This is where *Tohu* started: the *shevira* (breaking of the vessels) starts in *SaG* of *SaG*, *bina sheb'bina*, the root of all the kings, the real eighth king of *Tohu*, not the new *MaH* of repair. There they reasoned their way to wanting *chachma*, rising above *bina* and below it, through *daas*. His point: *bina sheb'bina* joins *bina* and *tevuna* through the straight *nun*.

blocks.question: So the shevira is in the uvchein?
blocks.text: Yes, the *shevira* is in the *uvchein*. He says there is no *shevira* in *bina* itself, but there is: it is in the *middos* of *bina*, the decision reached. In the *Chabad* of *bina*, *bina sheb'bina*, there is no real *shevira*, but that is its source.

Two people can agree on the whole analysis of a problem in the world and draw opposite conclusions from it. Take the pro-choice people: in their analysis there seem to be famines in the world, and overpopulation, and gangs and stuff like that. That is true; I agree with that. So what should we do? I would say, well, we should study *Chassidus*. They say, well, let's kill all the babies. The *uvchein* is where the *shevira* is.

sensitivity.reason: Sums up the pro-choice position as "let's kill all the babies".
sensitivity.publishable: Two people can agree on the whole analysis of a problem in the world and draw opposite conclusions from it: one says, well, we should study *Chassidus*, and the other draws a destructive conclusion. The *uvchein* is where the *shevira* is.

blocks.text: The go-between is the straight *nun*, the length of *bina*: the *hisbonenus* itself; *chachma* of *bina*, new things, is the width. *Kelita* comes from going over the same explanation; deciding you understood and moving to another *Bava* is width, and brings none.
*Kelita* comes from learning this book again: as any college student knows, you reread the same length, not go off to the width.
So far: in chapter one *bina sheb'bina* activates the powers above it; now *daas*, *ben u'vas*, is activated by *tevuna*, and *tevuna* by *bina sheb'bina*, going over the length once more.

Hence *Tanya*'s one who serves G-d and one who did not: a hundred and one times against a hundred. Besides the effort beyond habit, it is *avoda* against *haskala*: the hundred and first time made him an *oved*, bringing *daas* into the thing and the thing into his *middos*.

By then he already understood it; that is where *kelita* starts. Learned it a hundred times? Very good: you are a *maskil*, not an *oved*, with no *daas* in it and no *middos* aroused, nothing brought down into *avoda*. "And this is enough for one who understands."

reviewQuestions.question: How does *tevuna* come about, and why does understanding a matter really well not yet give it?
In the deep well, what does the man of *bina* do, and what does the man of *tevuna* do? Who are the sheep here?
What do the Greeks' steam turbine and Archimedes' eureka show about *bina* and *tevuna*?
Why can someone who understands every *sevara* of a *pilpul* still be unable to rule guilty or innocent, and what did the Rambam have that he lacks?
Why is *tevuna* the lower mother of the *middos*, and *bina* in a way only the grandmother?
How does *bina sheb'bina* bring a person from *bina* to *tevuna*, and what does this have to do with learning a matter a hundred and one times?

His point about why tevuna 'was left' and bina is 'pretty much gone' is reported as he said it; the thread is loose in the recording and worth a listen.
'Shasik Rav' (019 11:21-12:01): he uses it for Rav deciding without giving the explanation; in the Gemara the phrase usually means Rav had no answer. Left as he said it.
